newsitem.title: USA: Saudi oil minister keeps low profile on U.S. visit.
newsitem.headline: Saudi oil minister keeps low profile on U.S. visit.

text.p: Saudi Arabian oil minister Ali Naimi is keeping a low profile on his visit to Washington as part of a high ranking Saudi delegation led by deputy prime minister and defense minister Prince Sultan.
He refused to answer any questions upon leaving a luncheon hosted Thursday by U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.
"You might as well give up on this trip," he said.
Naimi was unavailable on Wednesday, and declined to make any statement to reporters Tuesday following a meeting with his U.S. counterpart, Acting Energy Secretary Charles Curtis.
Curtis said Thursday they had agreed not to make any statements because they were "sensitive" about upstaging the defense minister's visit.
Naimi is due to attend meetings at the Saudi embassy Friday before the delegation leaves.

The Saudi delegation arrived in Washington Monday for talks with President Clinton and key new cabinet members to discuss issues ranging from Saudi defense needs to the Middle East peace process and oil markets.

Close U.S.-Saudi ties have been rattled in recent months by U.S. complaints that Riyadh was not sharing enough information on its investigation into last June's truck bombing that killed 19 American servicemen in Dhahran.
The Saudi ministers Thursday renewed pledges to cooperate with the United States in the investigation.
